pk.s: Lead-spacing about 10 to 12.5 mm on a PCB

typ: Values follow the E12, E24 (5 %) and E96 (1 %) series
THT power ratings: 0.25 W, 0.5 W, 1 W, 2 W are common
items.mark: THT: colour bands (use the Resistor colour code tool). SMD: 3-digit (103 = 10 kΩ), 4-digit (1002 = 10 kΩ) or EIA-96 (01C = 10 kΩ) markings (use the SMD code decoder).
items.test: Measure resistance with the circuit de-energised and one lead lifted. The reading should be within tolerance.

pk.s: Larger ceramic or metal-clad bodies for 5 W and above

typ: Power from a few watts to hundreds of watts
Used for braking, loads, current sensing and inrush limiting
Mounts with clearance, because it gets hot
items.mark: Value and power are printed on the body, for example 10R 10W.
items.test: Measure resistance cold, with one lead lifted. Check for discolouration and cracks.
items.note: Rated power is only valid with the cooling the maker specifies.

pk.s: Outer pins are the ends of the track; the middle pin is the wiper

typ: Total resistance 1 kΩ to 1 MΩ typical
Linear (B) and logarithmic (A) tapers
items.mark: Value and taper on the body: 10K B = 10 kΩ linear. A 103 trimmer is 10 kΩ.
items.test: Between the outer pins you should read the total resistance; between the wiper and an outer pin it should change smoothly as you turn it.

pk.s: Typically 0.1 µF (104) is the common bypass value

typ: pF to a few µF; voltage ratings 6.3 V to 1 kV
Dielectrics: C0G/NP0 stable; X7R, X5R moderate; Y5V changes a lot with temperature and voltage
items.mark: 3-digit pF code: 104 = 10 × 10⁴ pF = 100 nF. A letter after the code is tolerance (J ±5 %, K ±10 %, M ±20 %). SMD MLCCs are usually unmarked.
items.test: Use a capacitance meter. A short-circuited capacitor reads near 0 Ω.

pk.s: Stripe marks the negative lead; on new parts the long lead is positive
Stripe or black mark on the top marks the negative side

typ: About 1 µF to many thousands of µF; ratings from 6.3 V to 450 V
Polarised; ESR and ripple current limit life
items.mark: Capacitance (µF) and voltage are printed on the can. The stripe marks the negative terminal.
items.test: Use a capacitance or ESR meter. Look for a bulging or leaking top.
items.note: Reverse polarity or over-voltage can make it fail violently.

pk.s: The stripe or bar marks the POSITIVE end

typ: About 0.1 µF to a few hundred µF, 2.5 V to 50 V (typical)
Polarised; sensitive to surge current and reverse voltage
items.mark: Value and voltage on the body (for example 106 6V = 10 µF, 6.3 V). The bar marks positive.
items.test: Capacitance meter. A short circuit means it has failed.
items.note: Unlike aluminium electrolytics, the stripe marks positive.

pk.s: Common in filters, motor run and mains circuits

typ: nF to µF; 63 V to 1000 V or more
Safety types X2 (across the line) and Y2 (line to earth) are used in mains filters
items.mark: Value in µF or a 3-digit code on the body (104 = 100 nF), with voltage rating.
items.test: Capacitance meter; check for swelling or burn marks.

pk.s: Bands follow the resistor code, value in µH

typ: µH to mH; ratings include current and saturation current
DC resistance (DCR) matters for losses
items.mark: SMD: 100 = 10 µH, 4R7 = 4.7 µH. Axial: colour code in µH.
items.test: An LCR meter measures inductance. A multimeter shows a low DC resistance (a good winding).

typ: Specified by impedance at 100 MHz and rated current
Used to suppress high-frequency noise
items.mark: Often unmarked; the datasheet gives impedance at 100 MHz.
items.test: A multimeter should show a very low resistance.

pk.s: Primary and secondary pins are on opposite sides

typ: Primary and secondary voltages, VA rating
Mains types isolate the secondary from the line
items.mark: The label shows primary and secondary voltages and VA.
items.test: Measure each winding resistance (continuity). A step-down transformer has a higher resistance on the primary.
items.note: Mains voltage is dangerous; never test a transformer on live mains with a meter.

typ: Rated current, rated voltage and breaking capacity
Fast-blow (F) and time-delay (T) types
items.mark: Current and voltage printed on the end cap (for example T 2A 250V).
items.test: Continuity test: a good fuse reads about 0 Ω.
items.note: Replace only with the same type and rating.

pk.s: Placed across the line to absorb surges

typ: Protects against voltage surges
Rated by varistor voltage and energy
items.mark: 14D471K: 14 mm disc, 471 = 47 × 10¹ = 470 V (varistor voltage), K = ±10 %.
items.test: A good MOV reads open on the ohm range. A reading near 0 Ω means it has failed.
items.note: Failed MOVs can overheat; replace the whole protected device if they are scorched.

pk.s: Used for sensing and inrush limiting

typ: Often specified as R25, for example 10 kΩ at 25 °C
Resistance falls as temperature rises
items.mark: Value at 25 °C printed or in the datasheet (10K = 10 kΩ).
items.test: Measure at room temperature (near its R25), then warm it with your fingers; the resistance should drop.

pk.s: Two pads are usually unused ground pads

typ: Frequency (for example 8 MHz, 16 MHz, 32.768 kHz)
Load capacitance matters for accuracy
items.mark: The frequency is printed on the can.
items.test: A multimeter cannot test it; use an oscillator circuit or oscilloscope.

typ: SPDT contacts; common small types are rated about 10 A at 250 V AC (check the label)
Needs a flyback diode across a DC coil
items.mark: Coil voltage and contact ratings are printed on the case.
items.test: Measure the coil resistance; apply the rated coil voltage and listen for a click; check contacts with continuity.

pk.s: Pins on the same side are joined inside

typ: Momentary push button
Low-current signal switch
items.mark: No marking; check the datasheet for the pin layout.
items.test: Continuity between the pins across the button should appear only when pressed.

typ: Pitch 2.54 mm (0.1 in)
Current per pin is low (about 1 A, check the datasheet)
items.mark: No marking.
items.test: Check continuity from each pin to the pad.

typ: Forward drop about 0.7 V
items.mark: The stripe marks the cathode.
items.test: Diode-test mode: about 0.5 to 0.7 V one way and OL the other.

pk.s: Same function in a smaller package

typ: Fast switching, up to about 100 V (1N4148)
Forward drop about 0.7 V
items.mark: Black band = cathode.
items.test: Diode-test mode as for any silicon diode.

typ: Low forward drop, about 0.2 to 0.4 V
Fast switching; used in power supplies
items.mark: The stripe marks the cathode.
items.test: Diode-test mode shows a lower forward reading than a silicon diode.

typ: Regulates at its Zener voltage in reverse bias
Power ratings 0.5 W, 1 W and higher
items.mark: Voltage is often printed, for example 5V1 = 5.1 V.
items.test: Diode-test mode shows it as a normal diode forward. Its Zener action needs a supply and series resistor.

pk.s: Long lead = anode; flat side of the body = cathode

typ: Forward voltage about 1.8 to 2.2 V (red, yellow, green) and 2.8 to 3.6 V (blue, white)
Typical current 5 to 20 mA; always use a series resistor
items.mark: No value marking. Cathode marks vary on SMD LEDs; check the datasheet.
items.test: Diode-test mode may light it dimly.

pk.s: 45 V, 100 mA; with the flat face toward you, pins left to right are C, B, E

typ: Current gain β (hFE), collector current and voltage ratings
Pinouts differ between types: always check the datasheet
items.mark: The type number is printed on the body, for example BC547.
items.test: Diode-test mode: base to emitter and base to collector each read about 0.6 V with the red probe on the base, and OL the other way.

typ: Same ratings idea as NPN with reversed polarities
items.mark: The type number is printed on the body.
items.test: Diode-test mode with the black probe on the base reads about 0.6 V to the other pins.

pk.s: IRF540N: 100 V, 33 A; IRFZ44N: 55 V, 49 A

typ: Key ratings: Vds, Id, Rds(on), gate threshold Vgs(th)
Logic-level types switch fully at about 4.5 to 5 V
items.mark: The type number is printed on the body.
items.test: Handle with ESD care. A good device is open between drain and source with a diode drop from source to drain; near 0 Ω between pins means shorted.

pk.s: Common for 600 V to 1200 V devices

typ: Used in inverters, VFDs and welders
Rated by Vce, Ic and switching speed
items.mark: The type number is printed on the body.
items.test: Handle with ESD care. A shorted device reads near 0 Ω between collector and emitter.

pk.s: Anode usually connects to the tab; check the datasheet

typ: Latches on after a gate pulse and turns off when the current falls below the holding current
Used in controlled rectifiers and motor drives
items.mark: The type number is printed on the body.
items.test: Anode to cathode reads open both ways; the gate to cathode shows a low resistance or diode-like reading.

typ: Switches AC in both directions
Used in dimmers and small motor controls
items.mark: The type number is printed on the body.
items.test: MT1 to MT2 reads open both ways; the gate to MT1 reads a low resistance.

typ: Heat dissipated = (Vin − Vout) × I
Check the dropout voltage and the datasheet pinout
items.mark: Fixed regulators show the output voltage in the number (7805 = 5 V).
items.test: Measure the input and output voltage on a powered, current-limited supply; check for overheating.

typ: LM358 dual, works from a single supply
Pin 1 is next to the dot or notch
items.mark: The type number is on the top. A dot or notch marks pin 1.
items.test: Check supply and output voltages in a powered circuit.

typ: Astable frequency f ≈ 1.44 / ((R1 + 2 × R2) × C)
Monostable pulse width about 1.1 × R × C
items.mark: Type number and date code on top; the dot or notch marks pin 1.
items.test: Check in a powered circuit with an oscilloscope on the output.

pk.s: No leads; pads under the body

typ: Check supply voltage, clock and I/O ratings in the datasheet
Many parts need ESD care
items.mark: A dot or notch marks pin 1. The type number is on top.
items.test: Check supply, reset and clock on a powered board.

pk.s: Input LED side and output transistor side

typ: Isolates the input from the output
Current transfer ratio (CTR) sets how much output current you get
items.mark: Type number on top; the dot marks pin 1 (LED anode on the PC817).
items.test: Diode-test the LED side; the output transistor reads open until the LED is driven.

typ: Rated by current and reverse voltage, for example 2 A to 35 A, 100 V to 1000 V
Needs a heat sink at higher currents
items.mark: Pins are marked ~ (AC in) and + − (DC out).
items.test: Diode-test between pins: each diode in the bridge should read about 0.5 to 0.7 V one way.
